executive_summary: The Swiss franc enters October 2026 at its weakest level against the US dollar in sixteen months, with USD/CHF at 0.83375 and EUR/CHF at 0.94562 on the gated price store's 2026-09-29 close [1][9]. On an inverted convention where a rising pair means a weaker franc, CHF has lost 3.04% against USD over one month, 3.62% over three, 4.27% over six and 3.92% over twelve, and the Swiss National Bank itself put the trade-weighted depreciation at approximately 3% since June [2]. The dominant narrative is the simplest one available: an energy shock drove global headline inflation to 3.4% in the United States and 3.2% in the euro area and set off a synchronised tightening cycle across nine of CHF's ten peers - the Bank of Japan, Norges Bank and the RBA all hiked in the twelve days to 2026-09-29 [21] - while Swiss headline inflation rose only to 0.8% and core to 0.4% because energy is roughly 3.5% of the Swiss basket against about 7% in the eurozone [6][35][36]. The SNB consequently held at 0.00% on 2026-09-24 for a fifth consecutive meeting, leaving the franc the lowest-yielding currency in G10+SGD by 125bp (against the Bank of Japan's 1.25%) and 387.5bp below the Fed, with the USD/CHF futures roll at -457.8bp annualised [1][5]. Valuation does not contradict the move: the BIS real effective rate at 99.87 for 2026-08 is 2.83% below its year-earlier level and ranks seventh of eleven, so this is a cheapening currency rather than an expensive one being corrected. The central tension is that Switzerland pairs the second-largest current account surplus in the block at 9.198% of GDP and the fastest quarterly growth at 1.885% with the lowest policy rate and the lowest core inflation [4][14], and that the market prices roughly 75bp of SNB tightening by September 2027 against an SNB conditional forecast of 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% built explicitly on an unchanged 0% rate and an economist consensus of no move before 2028 [1][5][6]. We are Bearish CHF on both horizons - conviction 3, tactical net score -0.3002 and strategic -0.2566 - with the caveat that the single largest driver of the view, the market's SNB hike pricing, is also the thing most likely to be wrong, and the franc's fat-tailed response to a genuine risk event caps how far the position should be pressed.

valuation.trade_weighted_assessment: The franc's trade-weighted position is mid-pack and deteriorating: 99.87 against AUD at 116.11, SGD at 114.81 and GBP at 112.33, with only CAD (96.29), SEK (94.83) and JPY (66.02) lower. The SNB's own characterisation of an approximately 3% trade-weighted depreciation since June 2026 is consistent with the 2.83% one-year REER decline and confirms that the easing of Swiss monetary conditions has come through the exchange rate rather than the policy rate [2].
valuation.what_is_priced_in: A franc at 99.87 in real effective terms prices neither a safe-haven premium nor a crisis discount - it prices the absence of an event. The market is also pricing roughly 75bp of SNB tightening by September 2027 and nearly a 50% chance of a hike at the 2026-12-10 assessment [6], which is the one piece of the valuation that looks rich: it sits against an SNB conditional forecast of 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% constructed on an unchanged 0% rate [1] and a Swiss Bankers Association survey in which 60% of respondents see no change through 2027 [5]. What is NOT priced is any revaluation of Switzerland's 9.198%-of-GDP current account surplus, which the forward curve treats purely as a carry differential.
valuation.actionability: The valuation signal is structural, not actionable: a REER within 0.13 points of its base period generates no mean-reversion trigger at either horizon. The actionable valuation observation is the PPP-proxy dispersion - CHF is 13.99% cheap against AUD and 13.01% cheap against SGD in relative real terms while 5.31% expensive against SEK and 3.72% expensive against CAD - which argues for expressing a franc view in the crosses where the real-rate gap has already done its work rather than against the dollar alone.

positioning_summary.interpretation: Open interest tells the more interesting story than the net. Between 2026-08-18 and 2026-09-15 open interest rose from 113,749 to 171,313 contracts, a 50.6% expansion, and then fell 37,818 contracts or 22.1% in the single week to 2026-09-22 while leveraged funds still added shorts. Position consolidation of that shape - weaker hands leaving, the directional net extending - leaves a more concentrated and more fragile short book than the headline -16,457 suggests. Dealers are the offset at +68,285 net long, the largest dealer long in the cached sample.
positioning_summary.contrarian_assessment: This is the clearest CHF-bullish signal in the dossier and it is why Factor 4 is Bullish tactically against nine other factors. A leveraged net short at -12.3% of open interest with open interest down 22.1% in a week is the configuration that produces squeezes, and the currency brief's own warning is that CHF positioning extremes are smaller than EUR or JPY because open interest is lower, so -16,457 contracts carries more price impact per contract than the absolute number implies. The qualification is that the vendor all-speculator net has ALREADY trimmed from -30.0K to -26.8K over two weeks without the franc rallying - shorts were reduced into franc weakness, which means the squeeze fuel is being spent without a squeeze. That is why the stance is Bullish at 60 rather than at 70.

market_context.recent_regime: The regime is a globally synchronised tightening cycle driven by an energy shock that barely touches Switzerland, and the franc is the funding leg. Brent at approximately USD 100 is 56.2% higher over twelve months, and the Fed, ECB, BoJ, BoE, BoC, RBA, RBNZ, Norges Bank and Riksbank - nine of the ten peers - have tightened or are expected to tighten within six months, with the BoJ, Norges Bank and the RBA all hiking between 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-29 [21][30], while Swiss headline inflation at 0.8% and core at 0.4% give the SNB no reaction-function reason to follow [28][35][36]. Price action is a low-volatility grind: USD/CHF trades 26 pips below a sixteen-month high while 20-day realised vol has fallen to 5.25% from a 60-day 7.10%. The dominant narrative is carry, not risk: VIX at 16.07 and the S&P 500 up 14.33% year to date deny the franc any safe-haven bid, while high-yield spreads 42bp wider over the month and an OAT-Bund spread at a one-year high of 111.2bp show the repricing is happening in rates rather than in fear [29][32]. The volatility state is therefore benign in the body and fat-tailed at the edges, with two live binaries - an Iran war on day 215 and a French budget vote - either of which would convert the regime in a session.

base_currency.expected_action: Hold at 0.00% at the quarterly monetary policy assessment, against a market pricing nearly a 50% chance of a 25bp hike [6]. Our expectation is a hold with no tightening signal, because the SNB's own conditional forecast of 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% for 2026-2028 is constructed on an unchanged 0% rate and already sits inside the 0-2% band [1], core inflation is 0.40% and nominal wage growth is 0.40% [8][10][35]. The meeting is 70 days after the valuation date and is the only scheduled SNB communication inside either horizon - only four assessments a year means each carries outsized weight and the gaps between them are the longest guidance vacuums in G10.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the question is not the level of the differential but its direction, and here the honest answer is that it stops widening. The Fed is expected to deliver one more 25bp hike to 4.00-4.25% and then pause, with the 2Y at 4.89-4.92% already embedding roughly 102-105bp above the current midpoint - so most of the US tightening is in the price rather than ahead of it [7][25]. The ECB has delivered its hike, explicitly states it 'is not pre-committing to a particular rate path', and its own projections take HICP from 3.0% in 2026 to 2.1% in 2028, which is a cycle ending rather than extending [23]. The late-September decisions qualify that read without overturning it: the Bank of Japan, Norges Bank and the RBA all hiked 25bp between 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-29, so peers are still delivering, but Norges Bank at 4.50% and the RBA at 4.60% are both expected to hold at their November meetings, and the BoJ - the peer closest to the franc - would only WIDEN CHF's 125bp disadvantage if the Reuters-polled 1.75% by Q2 2027 materialises [21][28]. On the Swiss side the mechanical effect of the market's 75bp of hike pricing is that CHF's measured carry disadvantage narrows through the horizon even if the SNB never moves, because forward differentials already embed it. Against that, the SNB has four meetings a year and only one falls inside the horizon, so the probability-weighted amount of Swiss policy news available between now and March 2027 is small, and the 0.00% floor means the SNB cannot ease to defend the franc's competitiveness without going negative, which neither the June nor the September documents even discuss [1][3]. The strategic stance stays Bearish because a 387.5bp dollar carry and a 250bp euro carry do not cease to bite over six months, but confidence falls from 77 to 66 because the second derivative has turned: the late-September hikes took Norges Bank and the RBA to levels both are expected to hold, and peers' tightening cycles are closer to their end than their beginning, and the one scheduled Swiss event inside the horizon is a coin-flip the market has already priced at 50%.

carry_analysis.carry_regime: Carry is working, and that is the regime's defining feature. VIX at 16.07, US investment-grade spreads at 83bp and the S&P 500 up 14.33% year to date describe an environment in which funding-currency shorts are rewarded rather than squeezed [29], and the franc has duly lost ground on eight of nine crosses over one month and all nine over three months. The regime breaks when realised volatility rises: the currency brief's fat-tail warning means CHF's carry-adjusted return distribution is negatively skewed, so the strategy earns steadily and loses violently, and at a 20-day realised vol of 5.25% on USD/CHF the market is sizing for the body of that distribution rather than its tail.

tactical.analysis: This factor is genuinely balanced and the stance is Neutral for that reason rather than for want of a view. The inflation side is unambiguously CHF-negative in its policy implication: headline CPI at 0.80% year on year in August 2026 is the second-lowest in G10+SGD behind Sweden's 0.30%, core at 0.40% is the LOWEST of the eleven, food prices are falling at 1.10% and producer and import prices at 0.70%, and nominal wage growth of 0.40% removes the persistence channel entirely [8][10][35]. The August rise from 0.40% to 0.80% was energy, and the SNB said so - 'inflation has risen further since June, primarily due to higher energy prices' - with energy only about 3.5% of the Swiss basket against roughly 7% in the eurozone, so the pass-through that pushed euro-area headline HICP to 3.20% and US CPI to 3.40% lifted Switzerland by 40bp [1][6]. The growth side is just as unambiguously CHF-positive: Q2 GDP grew 1.885% quarter on quarter, the fastest in the block, and 2.632% year on year, second only to Sweden; the KOF Economic Barometer printed 109.1 on 2026-09-29 against a 105.8 consensus, a five-year high and a 3.3-point beat, with the three-month path running 104.2 to 107.5 to 109.1; and the procure.ch manufacturing PMI at 57.1 beat a 54.1 forecast on the cached release calendar [12]. The September surprise tally is six positive and zero negative on the vendor's own economic-direction flag. Two things keep this from being a bullish read: SECO itself notes that roughly half of Q2 growth came from the volatile chemical-pharmaceutical sector and expects a second-half slowdown [13], and the ZEW expectations index collapsed from 12.1 to 2.6 on 2026-09-30, a 9.5-point fall that is the single clearest forward-looking negative in the Swiss data set and sits directly against KOF.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the inflation differential dominates the growth level, and the stance turns Bearish CHF. The mechanism is arithmetic: a central bank reaction function responds to the gap between inflation and target, and Switzerland's core at 0.40% against a 0-2% band midpoint is 160bp below where the euro area sits at 2.40% and the United States at 2.40%, so even if every central bank behaved identically the SNB would be last to move [35]. The SNB's own conditional forecast says exactly this, placing inflation at 0.7% in 2026 and 0.8% in both 2027 and 2028 on an unchanged rate [1], and SECO's panel independently forecasts 0.6% average inflation for both 2026 and 2027 [13]. The energy impulse that produced the August jump has plateaued rather than reversed: Brent at approximately USD 100 (USD 100.17 on 2026-10-01) is 4.75% higher over September and 56.2% higher over twelve months, while Middle East crude exports have recovered to just under 80% of their pre-war level, so it is base effects rather than a price decline that shrink energy's contribution to Swiss headline CPI over the horizon - a slower and less certain mechanism [30][31]. The growth story faces a harder test than its current level suggests. SECO raised 2026 to 1.7% from 0.9% but left 2027 at 1.6% and flagged that half of Q2 came from chemicals and pharmaceuticals, a sector whose quarterly contribution is notoriously lumpy, and KOF's own release names weakening foreign demand, declining financial and insurance services and employment prospects under pressure as offsets inside a headline beat [12][13]. Wage growth of 0.40% against the SNB's 1.5-2% GDP forecast is the tell: this is output growth without income growth, which does not generate domestic inflation. Confidence is 54 rather than higher because a Swiss economy growing at the fastest quarterly rate in the block with unemployment at 3.1% is not obviously a disinflationary machine, because energy near USD 100 is holding rather than falling, and because a second consecutive 0.8%-plus headline print would force a reassessment.

factors.horizon_split_explanation: Tactical is Neutral and strategic is Bearish because the two sides of this factor operate on different clocks. Over two to four weeks the growth data is loud - KOF at a five-year high, a PMI beat, six positive surprises and no negatives - and it genuinely offsets the disinflation case in the market's attention. Over one to six months the growth level cannot move the SNB's reaction function without wages or core inflation following, and neither is following at 0.40% apiece, so the 200bp core-inflation gap to the ECB and the Fed becomes the operative variable and the energy impulse that disguised it fades through base effects.

tactical.analysis: The franc's tactical problem is that the risk environment is exactly wrong for it. VIX at 16.07 on 2026-09-28 sits in the lower third of its historical distribution, up only 1.64 points from 14.43 four weeks earlier; the S&P 500 at 7,677.36 is up 14.33% year to date and within 1.8% of its August record of 7,816.70; and US investment-grade spreads at 83bp are historically tight [29]. CHF is a safe haven whose return depends on capital flight, and there is none - the mechanism that makes the franc work is simply not firing. The currency brief's own correlation table puts CHF against VIX at +0.2 to +0.4 and EUR/CHF against European equity indices at +0.2 to +0.4, both of which imply franc weakness in exactly this tape. The gold corroboration is unusually clean: XAU/USD at 4,181.99954 on 2026-09-29 is down 6.00% over one month, and since the brief identifies gold as CHF's commodity link through shared safe-haven demand rather than trade, a 6% gold decline alongside a 3.04% franc decline against the dollar is the same signal measured twice. Two counterweights exist and both are real. US high-yield spreads widened 42bp over the month from 2.60% to 3.02%, which is the credit market beginning to price the rate shock rather than ignoring it; and the OAT-Bund spread at 111.2bp on 2026-09-29 is at the very top of its one-year range of 59.0-111.2bp against a 74.2bp average, with French debt at 119% of GDP and a EUR 54bn budget vote pending [32]. The brief puts EUR/CHF against the BTP-Bund spread at -0.2 to -0.3, so eurozone sovereign stress is the live safe-haven channel. The stance is Bearish at 64 because the equity and volatility channels are decisively against the franc while the credit and sovereign-spread channels are only beginning to turn, and because CHF/JPY at the 21st percentile shows the market has been choosing the other safe haven when it wants one.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the stance is Neutral, and the shift from Bearish is a statement about convexity rather than about direction. The base rate for a volatility event inside six months is materially above zero and CHF's payoff to one is large and non-linear: the currency brief records the January 2015 floor removal moving EUR/CHF roughly 30% intraday, and its characterisation of CHF as a low-average-vol currency with a fat-tail problem is precisely a description of positive convexity for a long position. Two identifiable triggers sit inside the horizon. The first is the 2026 Iran war, on day 215 at 2026-09-30, where the United States has categorically rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap and the residual disagreement is over sequencing - a live negotiation that can fail as easily as succeed, with Middle East crude exports at just under 80% of their pre-war level and US diesel at a record USD 6.53 per gallon [31]. The second is France, where 111.2bp over Bunds, 119% debt to GDP and a EUR 54bn budget vote make a government collapse a genuine possibility, and where the franc rather than the euro is the regional refuge [32]. Against those, the structural case for a benign tape is strong: credit is tight at 83bp investment grade, equities are 14.33% higher year to date, and the Fed is tightening into an economy with 4.1% unemployment rather than easing into a recession. The resolution is that the distribution is wide and roughly symmetric in expectation but asymmetric in shape - most paths deliver no franc bid and a minority deliver a large one - which is the definition of a Neutral stance with real content. Confidence is 56 because the weight on this factor falls to 0.05 strategically and because the correlation regime itself is in question: gold down 6.00% while VIX rose 1.64 points is not the standard risk-off/risk-on structure, and a broken correlation regime is a reason to claim less, not more.

factors.horizon_split_explanation: The divergence is mechanical and comes from the horizon's exposure to tail events rather than from any change in the base case. Over two to four weeks the probability that a volatility regime shift occurs and completes is low, so the franc simply pays its carry into a calm tape and the stance is Bearish. tactical.analysis: Positioning is the one factor arguing for the franc and it argues for it on specifics rather than on sentiment. Leveraged funds are net short 16,457 CHF contracts in the week ending 2026-09-22, the fifth consecutive week of short building from 8,825 on 2026-08-25 - an 86% increase in the net short over five weeks - and at 12.3% of open interest that is the most stretched reading in the cached 2026-04-07 to 2026-09-22 sample [15]. Asset managers are short 35,523, a position that has been stable in the 28,655-37,070 range since mid-August, so the directional conviction is coming from the fast money rather than from real money. Dealers hold the offset at +68,285 net long, the largest dealer long in the sample. The important number is open interest: it rose from 113,749 on 2026-08-18 to 171,313 on 2026-09-15, a 50.6% expansion, and then fell 37,818 contracts or 22.1% in the single week to 2026-09-22 while leveraged funds still added shorts. A 22% collapse in open interest alongside an extending directional net is position consolidation - weaker hands leaving and the surviving book concentrating - which leaves the short more fragile than its absolute size implies. The currency brief's threshold is instructive here: it sets CHF's contrarian level at plus or minus 30,000 net spec contracts precisely because CHF open interest is far smaller than EUR's or JPY's, so price impact per contract is higher. The vendor all-speculator series touched exactly 30,000 short on 2026-09-11 before easing to 29,000 and then 26,800 by the 2026-09-25 release [15]. strategic.analysis: Over one to six months positioning carries no directional signal and the stance is Neutral. The reason is structural rather than cyclical: the currency brief records that CHF positioning 'tends to be structurally short, as a carry funding currency, with sharp short-covering rallies during risk-off', so a net short is the franc's resting state and not an anomaly to be mean-reverted. Across the full cached sample from 2026-04-07 the leveraged net has been short in every single tranche, ranging from -8,825 to -16,457, and the asset-manager net from -28,655 to -37,070 - there is no observation of a long position to revert toward. A six-month horizon is also long enough for the positioning to rebuild after any squeeze, so the information content decays: a squeeze in November that lifts the franc 2% does not change the carry arithmetic that put the short on, and with a 387.5bp dollar carry and a 250bp euro carry the short gets rebuilt. The weight falls from 0.10 to 0.06 for exactly this reason. Three things could make positioning a strategic signal rather than noise. First, a flip to net long by leveraged funds, which has not occurred in the cached sample and would mark a regime change in the franc's role. Second, a sustained SNB intervention programme visible as a multi-week sight-deposit build of more than CHF 5bn a week, which would put an official bid under EUR/CHF and compress the franc's upside - the opposite signal from the tactical one. Third, the SNB turning seller of reserves, visible as a sight-deposit fall of more than CHF 10bn over four weeks, which would be an official bid for francs. None of the three is present: reserves rose CHF 12.0bn in August to CHF 901.6bn but gold fell 6.00% and equities rose over the same period, so the increase is more plausibly valuation and investment income than franc selling. CHF's 0.19% share of allocated global reserves, flat over five years, confirms that reserve managers are neither accumulating nor abandoning the franc [17].

factors.horizon_split_explanation: Tactical is Bullish CHF and strategic is Neutral because contrarian positioning signals have a half-life measured in weeks. Over two to four weeks a leveraged net short at the sample extreme of 12.3% of open interest, with open interest down 22.1% in a single week, is a genuine asymmetry: the covering flow is concentrated and the liquidity to absorb it has left. Over one to six months the same short is the franc's structural resting state as a funding currency - short in every tranche of the cached sample - and any squeeze is followed by a rebuild at a 387.5bp dollar carry, so the signal decays to nothing and the weight is cut from 0.10 to 0.06 accordingly.
factors.contrarian_analysis_tactical: Positioning is stretched by the measure that matters for CHF. The leveraged net short at 12.3% of open interest is the sample extreme, and the currency brief's threshold of plus or minus 30,000 net spec contracts - set low precisely because CHF open interest is far smaller than EUR's or JPY's, so price impact per contract is higher - was touched at exactly -30,000 on 2026-09-11. The unwind trigger is specific: a failure of the Iran negotiation that lifts Brent back above USD 110, a French government collapse on the EUR 54bn budget vote that takes OAT-Bund through 125bp, or a VIX close above 24, any of which flips the risk channel and forces the fast money to cover into a market whose open interest has already fallen 22.1%. A squeeze from here would be violent by construction: the currency brief's analogue is the January 2015 floor removal, when EUR/CHF moved roughly 30% intraday, and while nothing of that order is in prospect, the structural point stands that CHF covering flows meet thin liquidity. The other side of the trade is being taken by dealers at +68,285 net long, the largest in the sample, and by the real-money accounts whose 35,523 short has stopped growing - the fast money is extending a position the slow money has stopped adding to, which historically marks the late innings rather than the early ones.
factors.contrarian_analysis_strategic: Strategically the contrarian case is weak and it is important to say so rather than to manufacture symmetry. CHF has been net short in every tranche of the cached sample and the brief describes that as its structural condition as a funding currency, so 'stretched' has no stable reference point at a six-month horizon - the distribution of CHF positioning is one-sided by construction. The contrarian case that does have content is about the SNB rather than the speculative community: the one agent capable of taking the other side of a 52,000-contract combined short at scale is the central bank, and its reaction function is asymmetric. It intervenes to cap franc STRENGTH, not weakness, so a weakening franc removes rather than adds an official bid - which is why the June 2026 'increased' willingness to intervene was dropped from the September language [2][3]. The genuine strategic contrarian risk is therefore the mirror image of a squeeze: if the franc weakens far enough that imported inflation becomes a Swiss problem, the SNB's own tolerance for depreciation ends, and UBS economists have already named that channel in warning that the depreciation 'could heighten concerns that inflation may accelerate beyond prior expectations' [6]. That is a limit on the trade rather than a reversal of it.

tactical.analysis: Switzerland's external position is the strongest in the block among non-resource economies and it transmits to spot on a timescale far longer than two to four weeks, which is why the tactical stance is Neutral. The level is not in doubt: the current account surplus ran 9.198% of GDP in 2026-Q2 on the pipeline vintage, second of eleven behind only Norway's petroleum-driven 19.614%, and the SNB's own release puts the quarterly surplus at CHF 24bn, up CHF 13bn year on year, with the net international investment position at CHF 986bn after a CHF 22bn quarterly gain [4]. The Q2 trade surplus nearly doubled to CHF 23.7bn from CHF 13.8bn a year earlier, with a goods surplus near CHF 30bn against a services deficit of CHF 4.4bn, exports up 5.5% as reported and roughly 8.8% seasonally adjusted at CHF 73.2bn, the third-highest on record [14]. Three things stop this being a tactical positive. First, the monthly trade balance released 2026-09-17 narrowed to CHF 3.786bn from CHF 5.742bn, so the high-frequency series is deteriorating even as the quarterly one improves. Second, the composition is distorted: precious metals accounted for 39.9% of 2025 goods exports at USD 221bn against pharmaceuticals at 21.7%, and the SNB names the non-monetary gold trading balance as a swing factor in the quarterly account, so monthly readings carry a large non-economic component [18]. Third, a structural surplus that has persisted for decades is by definition already in the exchange rate - it is the reason the franc appreciated in real terms over that period - and it generates no new flow inside a four-week window. The commodity channel is also unusually clean to assess for CHF, because the currency has no direct commodity export exposure at all: the brief identifies COMEX gold as the relevant link through shared safe-haven demand rather than trade, and gold at 4,181.99954 is down 6.00% over one month, which is franc-negative on that reading.

strategic.analysis: At the strategic horizon this is the strongest single argument for the franc and the factor's weight rises from 0.06 to 0.16, which is why it is the one line in the strategic weighted score that is materially positive. A current account surplus of 9.198% of GDP is not a cyclical phenomenon: it is composed of a goods trade surplus from pharmaceuticals and precision manufacturing, a services surplus from financial services and commodity trading, and a large primary income surplus from a CHF 5,564bn stock of foreign assets, and each of the three is structurally entrenched [4][18]. That surplus is the mechanism behind the franc's multi-decade real appreciation, and nothing in the current data suggests it is eroding - the Q2 surplus widened by CHF 13bn year on year and the net international investment position reached CHF 986bn. The terms of trade are not improving on the energy leg. Switzerland imports energy and exports high-value manufactures, and Brent at approximately USD 100 is 4.75% higher over September and 56.2% higher over twelve months - a modest terms-of-trade drag for a net energy importer whose energy share is small, partly offset by producer and import prices running at -0.70% year on year [30]. No Swiss terms-of-trade index exists in the cache and none was located as a current series, so the direction is inferred from those two components and the inference is stated rather than dressed as a measurement. Trading-partner concentration is a modest risk: the United States at 21.9% of goods exports is the single largest market and Europe takes 49.6% in aggregate, so Swiss export performance is hostage to US trade policy and euro-area demand in a way that a 9.2% surplus disguises. Reserve-currency dynamics add nothing: CHF holds 0.19% of allocated global reserves, flat over five years, so there is no allocation trend to ride [17]. Confidence is 68 - the highest directional confidence on the strategic horizon - because the surplus is measured rather than forecast, and the only question is timing, not existence; it is held below 70 because the energy leg of the terms of trade is a drag rather than a gain.

tactical.analysis: The gap between what the SNB says and what the market believes IS this factor, and it is unusually wide. The SNB published a conditional inflation forecast of 0.7% for 2026 and 0.8% for both 2027 and 2028 on 2026-09-24, built on the explicit assumption that the policy rate remains at 0%, and stated that monetary policy 'is appropriate to keep inflation within the range consistent with price stability' [1][2]. The market reads that document and prices nearly a 50% chance of a hike at the very next meeting and at least 0.75% by September 2027 [6]. Those two things cannot both be right, and the SNB has given the market no reason to prefer its own reading: the bank provides minimal forward guidance by design, meets only four times a year, and decisions rest with a three-member Governing Board, so between assessments there is almost no information flow to resolve the disagreement. The one language change in September was franc-negative. In June the SNB said 'the risk of strong Swiss franc appreciation remains. If necessary, the SNB's willingness to intervene in the foreign exchange market should therefore remain INCREASED'; in September it reverted to the standard formulation, 'we are also willing to be active in the foreign exchange market as necessary to ensure appropriate monetary conditions', dropping the qualifier [2][3][5]. Removing an elevated-intervention flag while the franc depreciates is the central bank signalling comfort with a weaker currency. Economist consensus sides with the SNB rather than with the curve: a Swiss Bankers Association survey found 60% of respondents expect no change through 2027, with some forecasters placing the first hike in 2028 or later [5]. Credibility is high - the SNB has delivered on its forecasts and its inflation record is the best in the developed world - but the 2015 floor removal remains the market's reference for the possibility of an un-telegraphed reversal, which is why the curve prices optionality the SNB's words do not justify.

strategic.analysis: Strategically the same wedge persists and the weight on it almost doubles from 0.07 to 0.12, which makes the SNB's December communication the most consequential scheduled event for the franc in either horizon. Three outcomes are distinguishable. If the SNB holds and publishes a conditional forecast that again keeps inflation inside the band on an unchanged rate - our base case - the market's 75bp of 2027 tightening becomes very difficult to sustain, the Swiss 2Y retraces toward 0.15% and the franc weakens on the repricing alone. If the SNB holds but raises its forecast or references normalisation, the pricing is validated and the franc rallies. If the SNB hikes, the franc rallies hard and this dossier is wrong on its largest single input. The structural features all favour the first outcome. The SNB's mandate is price stability with 'due account of economic developments', its forecast horizon runs to 2028 at 0.8%, and the bank has an explicit institutional preference for using the exchange rate as a disinflationary and re-inflationary tool rather than the rate - which is why intervention sits alongside rates as a co-equal instrument in its own description of policy [1][2]. There is also a floor problem working in the franc's favour that deserves stating: at 0.00% the SNB has no conventional easing room without going negative, and neither the June nor the September documents discuss negative rates at all [1][3]. That means a franc that strengthens sharply would be met with intervention rather than cuts, which is a less credible deterrent than a rate cut and partly explains why the market retains hike optionality. Confidence is 60, two points below tactical, because a six-month window contains one SNB meeting whose outcome is a genuine coin flip on the market's own numbers, and because the SNB's communication sparseness means there is no intermediate signal to update on.

tactical.analysis: Two dated binaries inside the tactical window both resolve in the franc's favour if they resolve badly for the world, and the options market is not charging much for that exposure, which is why this factor is Bullish CHF despite a modest 0.05 weight. The first is the 2026 Iran war, at day 215 on 2026-09-30. Iran submitted a seven-day roadmap requiring an immediate end to hostilities, removal of the naval blockade, sanctions relief and release of frozen funds, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz within a week and a return to nuclear negotiations, and the United States rejected it categorically; indirect talks took place at the UN General Assembly and the remaining disagreement is reported to concern sequencing rather than substance [31]. Hormuz flows have recovered to roughly 9.719mn b/d in September and Middle East crude exports to 16.328mn b/d, just under 80% of the 19.513mn b/d pre-war February baseline, and US diesel hit a record USD 6.53 per gallon, 70% above pre-war levels. A failure of the negotiation re-closes that recovery. The second is France: the OAT-Bund spread at 111.2bp on 2026-09-29 is at the top of its one-year range of 59.0-111.2bp against a 74.2bp average, French debt is 119% of GDP, a EUR 54bn budget vote is pending, and the currency brief puts EUR/CHF against eurozone sovereign spreads at -0.2 to -0.3, making the franc rather than the euro the regional refuge [32]. Swiss domestic political risk is effectively nil - stable federal government, direct democracy, no federal election inside the horizon - and the Switzerland-EU Bilaterals III package signed 2026-03-02 is not a tactical factor, with parliamentary debate running through 2026 and expected entry into force only at end-2028 [33]. Event vol is measurable and modest: USD/CHF one-month implied at 6.740% against 20-day realised of 5.25% is a 1.49-point premium, which is cheap gamma for two live binaries rather than expensive insurance. The honest counterweight is that both binaries are more likely to resolve benignly than not - Brent near USD 100 rather than at a crisis spike says the market thinks so - which caps confidence at 56.

strategic.analysis: Over one to six months the stance is Neutral because both binaries become two-sided and the modal resolution is franc-negative. On Iran, the direction of travel is toward settlement rather than escalation: regional crude exports at 16.328mn b/d, just under 80% of the pre-war baseline - the highest since the war began - Saudi Arabia having restored half its East-West pipeline capacity, and a dispute reduced to sequencing rather than substance all point the same way [30][31]. A settlement would collapse the energy premium, which is doubly franc-negative: it removes the safe-haven bid and it removes the inflation impulse supporting SNB hike pricing at the same time. On France, a government collapse is a real possibility inside six months but the mechanism has been tested repeatedly since 2024 and the market's response function has attenuated - 111.2bp is a one-year high, not a crisis level, and the euro area has ECB tools that did not exist in 2012. The Switzerland-EU file matters more strategically than tactically but still not much: the Bilaterals III package updates four treaties and adds three covering transport, free movement, food safety, electricity and health, requires parliamentary approval and probably a referendum whose date is not set, and is expected to enter force only at end-2028 - so inside six months it generates headlines rather than flows [33]. Two structural event risks from the currency brief deserve naming even though neither is live. UBS is now the dominant Swiss bank after absorbing Credit Suisse in 2023, which makes any UBS-specific stress systemic for the franc; and Switzerland's adoption of EU sanctions against Russia has already tested the neutrality on which the safe-haven franchise rests. Confidence is 52, the lowest directional confidence in the dossier, which is the honest reflection of a factor whose content is entirely about the probability distribution of negotiations no participant controls.

tactical.analysis: Switzerland's fiscal position generates no FX signal in either direction and the honest assessment is Neutral at high confidence rather than a manufactured positive. The sovereign is rated AAA by S&P, Fitch, DBRS and Scope and Aaa by Moody's, all with Stable outlooks, with no agency action in the research window [19]. Confederation debt stood at 14.80% of GDP in 2025, down from 15.20% in 2024, with a federal budget balance of 0.00% of GDP, and is forecast at 15.30% in 2026 easing to 14.90% by 2028 [11]. On the broader IMF general-government measure - which includes cantons, communes and social security and is the figure comparable to peers - gross debt was 39.4% of GDP in 2025 and is projected at 38.5% in 2026, falling toward 33.5% by 2031, placing Switzerland 137th of 190 countries [20]. The constitutional debt brake caps structural deficits, which is why the balance is zero rather than merely small. The market's assessment of this is visible in the curve: the 10-year Confederation bond yields 0.58% and the 2-year 0.31%, which are the lowest sovereign yields in the developed world and contain no identifiable credit premium at all [8][9]. Bond supply is not a factor - a government running a balanced budget with declining debt has no issuance problem, and no auction stress has been reported. The relative comparison is striking and worth stating without letting it drive a stance: France carries 119% debt to GDP and pays 111.2bp over Bunds, the United States runs a 3.03%-of-GDP current account deficit with 30-year yields at 5.59%, and Switzerland pays 0.58% at ten years on 38.5% debt [25][32]. That is a quality differential, but quality differentials only move FX when they are repriced, and Swiss credit quality has not changed. Confidence is 80, the highest in the dossier, because the conclusion that this factor is immaterial is itself well evidenced.

tactical.what_is_priced: Nothing is priced because nothing is in question: a 0.58% ten-year yield on AAA paper from a balanced-budget sovereign is the market pricing the absence of credit risk. There is no plausible tactical catalyst - no scheduled rating review, no auction calendar stress, no fiscal event - so the factor contributes exactly 0.0000 to the tactical weighted score at a 0.04 weight. Our expectation matches the market's and we say so rather than inventing a divergence.

strategic.analysis: The strategic weight rises from 0.04 to 0.07 and the stance remains Neutral, because a factor with no directional content does not acquire one by being weighted more heavily. The debt trajectory is the clearest in the developed world: general government gross debt falling from 40.5% in 2024 to 39.4% in 2025 to 38.5% in 2026 and projected at 33.5% by 2031, against a constitutional debt brake that makes the path a rule rather than a forecast [20]. Fiscal space is therefore ample in the sense that matters least - Switzerland could stimulate and chooses not to - and the currency brief is correct that this factor 'is not material and should be assessed as not currently relevant unless an extraordinary event occurs'. Debt sustainability is not a question when ten-year funding costs 0.58% and the primary balance is zero; interest expense as a share of revenue is negligible by construction. The one strategic consideration worth articulating is the direction in which this factor could become live, and it is not through Swiss fiscal deterioration. It is through peer deterioration being repriced: if the French situation escalated into a genuine euro-area sovereign event, Swiss credit quality would be repriced relative to the euro area and the franc would gain - but that transmission runs through Factor 3 and Factor 7, where it is already counted, and double-counting it here would inflate the weighted score dishonestly. Equally, if a Swiss referendum mandated a large structural spending programme the debt brake would be the binding constraint, and no such initiative is pending inside the horizon. Confidence falls from 80 to 74 only because a six-month window is long enough for a rating agency to open a review on any sovereign, and because the IMF debt figure for 2026 is a projection rather than an outturn.

strategic.analysis: Strategically the weight falls to 0.03 and the stance stays Bearish CHF but at lower confidence, because the structure that drives the franc lower in the short run is also what caps it in the long run. factors.expression_assessment: The vol landscape argues for expressing a strategic short-franc view through optionality and a tactical one through spot, and the two tenors say so for different reasons. At the one-month tenor implied of 6.740% exceeds 20-day realised of 5.25% by 1.49 points, so near-dated options are expensive relative to delivered movement and a tactical view is more efficiently taken in spot, where the 387.5bp dollar carry pays roughly 27 pips a month in the position's favour rather than bleeding premium. At the three-month tenor the relationship inverts: implied of 6.662% sits 0.44 points below 60-day realised of 7.10%, so the market is underpricing the movement the pair has actually produced and a strategic expression bought at that level is cheap. The term structure is in mild contango - 6.740% at 41.7 days, 6.662% at 104.7 days, 6.934% at 195.7 days - with no backwardation and therefore no single date demanding to be positioned around, which means there is no timing argument for waiting past the 2026-10-28 FOMC. The decisive consideration is the franc's negative skew for a short position: carry accrues steadily and reverses violently, with the January 2015 precedent of a roughly 30% intraday EUR/CHF move as the reference, so a short-franc position sized on 5.25% realised volatility is sized on the body of a distribution whose tail is the part that matters. The honest limitation is that the 25-delta risk reversal, the one instrument that would reveal whether the market's hedging demand is for franc upside or downside, is unavailable at any tenor, so the skew judgement rests on the currency's documented history rather than on current pricing, and Factor 9's confidence is reduced on both horizons for it.

tactical.analysis: Global dollar conditions are tightening through rates while remaining orderly through plumbing, and that specific combination is the worst available for a funding currency. The Federal Reserve raised its target range to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 with interest on reserve balances at 3.90%, the primary credit rate at 4.00% and the overnight reverse repo offering rate at 3.75% [24]. The broad trade-weighted dollar index DTWEXBGS stood at 120.33 on 2026-09-25, up 1.884 points or 1.59% over one month from 118.4461, and the US 10-year rose 51bp over the month to 5.24% [25]. Plumbing shows no stress at all: SOFR printed 3.90% on 2026-09-28, exactly at interest on reserve balances, against an effective fed funds rate of 3.88%, and central bank liquidity swaps outstanding were USD 72mn - effectively nil, and the single cleanest indicator that no institution anywhere is paying up for dollars through official channels [26][27][28]. SOFR printing AT rather than below interest on reserve balances is a mild sign of reserve tightening at the margin and worth noting, and reserve balances fell USD 83.6bn in the week to 2026-09-23 to USD 2,930.2bn, down USD 72.0bn year on year [27]. The mechanism for CHF is direct and runs through the brief's own description: low Swiss rates mean the franc is borrowed and converted into higher-yielding assets globally, and that trade unwinds - lifting the franc - only when dollar liquidity tightens AND volatility rises. Dollar liquidity is tightening in price but not in availability, and volatility is not rising, so the carry trade is being paid rather than squeezed. On the dollar smile the United States sits firmly on the right-hand side - exceptionalism, with the Fed hiking into 4.1% unemployment - which is the quadrant in which the franc weakens against the dollar while holding better against lower-yielding peers, and CHF/JPY at the 21st percentile shows even that consolation is not being delivered.

We agree, and that agreement is bearish for the franc rather than neutral - the franc needs scarce dollars and rising volatility to perform, and it has neither. strategic.analysis: Strategically the weight rises slightly from 0.11 to 0.12 and the stance stays Bearish CHF at lower confidence, because the balance sheet is now working against a dollar squeeze even as the policy rate works for a strong dollar. The Fed's implementation note directs the Desk to increase System Open Market Account holdings through purchases of Treasury bills, to roll Treasury principal at auction and to reinvest agency paydowns into bills, with no runoff caps - quantitative tightening has ended and the portfolio is growing, with Treasury holdings up USD 356.6bn year on year to USD 4,558.3bn [24][27]. A central bank adding reserves is not a central bank that produces a dollar shortage, which removes the most powerful mechanism by which the franc appreciates. Against that, reserve balances have still fallen USD 72.0bn over the year to USD 2,930.2bn and USD 83.6bn in the latest week, and SOFR at 3.90% is printing at interest on reserve balances rather than below it, so the system is closer to the minimum comfortable level of reserves than the growing portfolio implies [26][27]. Year-end is the seasonal pressure point: balance-sheet constraints at the turn of the year historically widen cross-currency basis and squeeze funding currencies higher, and that falls inside the strategic horizon. The measurement problem is material and must be stated rather than papered over: no free quoted cross-currency basis exists for EUR/USD, JPY/USD, GBP/USD or CHF/USD, the one 2026-dated article located contains only illustrative 50-200bp stress ranges rather than market quotes and was rejected, so this factor's funding read rests on SOFR, interest on reserve balances, reserve balances, the balance sheet, swap-line usage and the broad dollar index alone. The USD/CHF futures roll of -457.8bp against a -387.5bp policy spread bounds basis and term effects jointly at 70.3bp without separating them. Confidence is 56 rather than higher principally for that gap.

tactical.rationale: At tactical weights the book is dominated by the rate and data channels: Policy & Rates at 0.24, Inflation & Growth at 0.18, USD Liquidity & Funding at 0.11 and Risk Appetite at 0.10 account for 0.63 of the weight, and three of those four are Bearish CHF while the fourth is Neutral. The weighted score of -0.3002 is therefore not a close call produced by offsetting extremes but the arithmetic of a book in which seven factors are Bearish or Neutral and only two - Flows & Positioning at +0.0600 and Event Risk at +0.0280 - argue the other way, against a single Policy & Rates contribution of -0.1848. Mapped to the conviction ladder, a net score between -0.20 and -0.40 corresponds to conviction 3, and -0.3002 sits in the middle of that band rather than at an edge. The factor interactions reinforce rather than conflict in the places that matter most. The lowest policy rate in G10+SGD by 125bp - a gap that widened by 25bp against each of the BoJ, Norges Bank and the RBA in late September (Factor 1) - is sustainable precisely because core inflation is the lowest in the block at 0.40% and nominal wage growth is 0.40% (Factor 2), and the absence of an SNB reaction function is itself what makes the guidance vacuum franc-negative (Factor 6), while a 16.07 VIX and 83bp investment-grade spreads deny the franc the only mechanism that overrides carry (Factor 3) and orderly dollar funding with USD 72mn of swap lines removes the squeeze channel (Factor 10). The one genuine conflict is positioning: a leveraged net short at 12.3% of open interest with open interest down 22.1% in a week is a real asymmetry, and it is the main reason the score is -0.30 rather than -0.40. What is priced versus what we expect defines the edge. The market prices nearly a 50% chance of an SNB hike on 2026-12-10 and at least 0.75% by September 2027, against an SNB conditional forecast of 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% built explicitly on an unchanged 0% rate and a Swiss Bankers Association survey in which 60% see no change through 2027; we expect the SNB to validate its own forecast, which would remove the 19bp of hike pricing the Swiss 2Y has added over the month. Forward markets separately price CHF appreciation of 4.58% annualised against the dollar as the mechanical offset to the carry, and we expect spot to move with the carry instead, making the whole forward discount the measurable edge - 113.9 pips at one month against a forward outright of 0.83061. The path of least resistance is a grind higher in USD/CHF through the sixteen-month high of 0.83590 into the five-touch 0.83750-0.84560 band, with EUR/CHF testing its 200-week average at 0.94833 for the first time in 380 weeks. Dated catalysts inside the window are the Swiss CPI and procure.ch PMI on 2026-10-01, Swiss unemployment on 2026-10-06, SNB reserves on 2026-10-07, the French budget vote in the second week of October, and the FOMC on 2026-10-28 followed by the ECB on 2026-10-29. Conviction rests on three things that are measured rather than forecast: a 387.5bp dollar carry, a 0.40% core inflation rate, and the absence of any scheduled Swiss policy event for 70 days. Actionability is high because the expression is liquid and the carry pays while waiting - approximately 27 pips a month against the dollar and 20 against the euro - but position size should respect that the franc's loss distribution is negatively skewed, with the January 2015 floor removal as the reference for how violently it reverses.

The factors conflict in a specific and interpretable way. Switzerland's current account surplus of 9.198% of GDP, second of eleven behind only Norway, with a net international investment position of CHF 986bn and a Q2 trade surplus that nearly doubled to CHF 23.7bn, is the structural force that has driven the franc's multi-decade real appreciation and it has not weakened (Factor 5). The resolution is that the surplus caps the depreciation rather than reversing it, which is a conviction-3 view and not a conviction-4 one. The edge is the same wedge seen through a longer lens: the market prices at least 0.75% of SNB policy rate by September 2027 and economists price zero, and the 2026-12-10 assessment is the only scheduled Swiss event inside the horizon at which that can resolve. If the SNB confirms its own forecast the Swiss 2Y retraces from 0.31% toward 0.15% and the franc weakens on the repricing alone; if it validates the market, this dossier is wrong on its largest input and the franc rallies. Swiss core at 0.40% with Brent merely holding near USD 100 rather than rising further is the mechanism that pushes the first outcome. Conviction rests on the measured carry and the measured core inflation; it is limited by the measured surplus and by the franc's fat tail. consensus_divergence.consensus_view: On the franc, consensus is clustered at EUR/CHF 0.95 for end-2026, a UBS target first set in late 2025 and reaffirmed on 2026-09-24, with a 0.9000 downside scenario if geopolitical risks persist and Swiss companies surveyed by UBS expecting approximately 0.9100; the publisher's own central scenario is consolidation in a 0.9330-0.9500 corridor through Q4 [22]. consensus_divergence.our_view: We expect EUR/CHF at 0.9500 within two to four weeks and 0.9580 by end-Q1 2027, and USD/CHF at 0.8420 and 0.8520 respectively. On the SNB we side with the economists against the curve and expect no change through 2027, but we draw the opposite FX conclusion from that call: because the market has embedded roughly 75bp of tightening in the Swiss front end, the SNB confirming its own forecast is franc-NEGATIVE, not neutral.
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Approximately 80 pips above the clustered EUR/CHF consensus at the six-month horizon (0.9580 against 0.9500), and approximately 480 pips above a stale January 2026 aggregated consensus that implied USD/CHF near 0.7750. On the SNB we are 75bp below market pricing for September 2027 and aligned with economist consensus.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Three reasons, in order of weight. First, consensus treats the SNB's no-change path as neutral for the franc when it is in fact the removal of a priced hike cycle: the Swiss 2Y has added 19bp over the month on that pricing, and an SNB that confirms its own 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% conditional forecast takes it back out. Second, consensus overweights the energy impulse as a basis for Swiss tightening - Brent near USD 100 is 4.75% higher over September and 56.2% higher on the year, yet Swiss headline CPI reached only 0.80% and core fell to 0.40% because energy is only about 3.5% of the Swiss basket, so even an energy shock of this size has not produced a Swiss inflation problem and base effects alone take headline back toward the SNB's 0.7% path. Third, the 0.95 EUR/CHF target has stood for ten months and treats the 200-week average at 0.94833 as a ceiling rather than a level to be broken; 380 weeks without a close above it makes the break significant rather than incremental, and consensus is anchored on a regime that has held since 2019 rather than on the carry arithmetic now in force.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: A short-franc position against the dollar earns approximately 345 pips or 4.13% over six months including carry, and against the euro approximately 242 pips including the 118-pip six-month carry. The larger payoff is in the Swiss front end: a 2Y retracing from 0.31% to 0.15% on an uneventful December assessment is a 16bp move in a market that has been one-way for a month.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If the SNB validates market pricing on 2026-12-10 the dossier is wrong on its largest single input, and the franc rallies through the dense six-touch USD/CHF support at 0.80161-0.80842 toward the 0.8050 adverse case - a 287.5-pip or 3.45% loss before carry. cross_horizon_consistency.summary: Both horizons are Bearish CHF at conviction 3, with the tactical net score at -0.3002 and overall confidence 65 against a strategic -0.2566 and confidence 60. The direction is consistent and the strength decays with horizon.
cross_horizon_consistency.divergence_explanation: The stances agree but their composition does not, and that is the informative part. The tactical -0.3002 is built with almost no opposing contribution - only +0.0880 of positive weighted contribution in total - while the strategic -0.2566 is the residual of -0.3654 negative against a single +0.1088 positive from External Balance, whose weight rises from 0.06 to 0.16. A net score assembled from agreement is more reliable than one assembled from offset, so the strategic view carries the same nominal conviction with genuinely lower confidence and a smaller warranted position size. Four factors change stance across the horizons: Inflation & Growth from Neutral to Bearish as the 200bp core-inflation gap outlasts the growth beat, Risk Appetite from Bearish to Neutral as tail events gain time to resolve, Flows & Positioning from Bullish to Neutral as contrarian signals decay, and External Balance from Neutral to Bullish as cumulative flows start to matter.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The 2026-12-10 SNB monetary policy assessment, 70 days after the valuation date. It is the only scheduled Swiss policy event inside either horizon and the point at which the market's roughly 75bp of embedded tightening either resolves or is confirmed.
cross_horizon_consistency.catalyst_for_transition: The transition from tactical to strategic runs through the resolution of the energy impulse and the SNB's response to it. With Brent holding near USD 100 rather than rising further, the energy contribution to Swiss headline CPI fades through base effects while core sits at 0.40%, eroding the inflation basis for the market's hike pricing, and the 2026-12-10 assessment is where the SNB either acknowledges that - taking the Swiss 2Y from 0.31% toward 0.15% and extending the franc's decline - or surprises by validating the curve, in which case the strategic view inverts before the tactical one has finished paying.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Hold the same direction at both horizons but express them differently. The tactical view is best taken in spot, because a one-month implied of 6.740% against 20-day realised of 5.25% makes near-dated options expensive while the 387.5bp carry pays approximately 27 pips a month to wait. The strategic view should carry optionality, because a three-month implied of 6.662% sits 0.44 points below 60-day realised of 7.10% and because the franc's fat tail - the January 2015 analogue is a roughly 30% intraday EUR/CHF move - means a pure spot position is short a cheap option it should be long.

factors_changed.reason: Stance unchanged on both horizons; confidence lowered on both. The ECB hiked 25bp on 2026-09-10, widening the SNB-ECB gap from 225bp to 250bp, which deepens the level of CHF's disadvantage - but the market has now embedded roughly 75bp of SNB tightening by September 2027 and the Swiss 2Y has risen 19bp over the month, so the measured differential narrows through the forward curve even as the spot gap widens. A view whose level strengthens while its direction of travel weakens warrants less confidence, not more. The BoJ (to 1.25%), Norges Bank (to 4.50%) and the RBA (to 4.60%) all hiked in the second half of September, widening CHF's disadvantage against each by 25bp, which is why confidence sits at 77 and 66 - still below the prior 82 and 76.

Changed on both horizons. Tactically the prior Bullish read has been diluted: headline CPI doubled from 0.4% in July to 0.8% in August, which on its own supports the hawkish case, but core FELL from 0.5% to 0.4% and nominal wage growth is 0.40%, so the rise is energy rather than persistence. Set against a KOF at a five-year high of 109.1 and six positive September surprises with no negatives, the forces now genuinely offset. Strategically the 200bp core gap to the ECB and the Fed turns the factor Bearish, at a confidence of 54 because Brent near USD 100 is holding rather than falling, so the energy fade relies on base effects.

Stances unchanged on both horizons. VIX rose from 14.51 to 16.07 and high-yield spreads widened 42bp to 302bp, both marginal moves toward a franc-friendlier tape, which is why tactical confidence fell 4 points; the OAT-Bund spread reaching a one-year high of 111.2bp is the new element and it supports the franc, but gold falling 6.00% over the month works the other way through the shared safe-haven channel.

Changed on both horizons, and the two changes are the same observation read at two speeds. The all-speculator net deepened from -19,900 to -26,800 contracts and the leveraged net reached -12.3% of open interest, the sample extreme, while open interest collapsed 22.1% in a single week - which makes the tactical squeeze case materially stronger than a month ago. Over six months the same short is the franc's structural resting state and will be rebuilt at a 387.5bp carry, so the strategic signal decays to Neutral.

Changed tactically, held strategically with slightly lower confidence. The monthly trade balance fell from CHF 8.1bn in July to CHF 3.786bn in the August release, more than halving the high-frequency external signal even as the quarterly current account surplus widened CHF 13bn year on year to CHF 24bn - so the tactical read no longer supports a Bullish stance while the structural read still does. Strategic confidence is 68 because Brent near USD 100, +4.75% over September, is a modest terms-of-trade drag for a net energy importer rather than a gain.

Stance unchanged on both horizons; confidence lowered materially on both. The SNB held at 0% on 2026-09-24 and reverted from June's 'increased' willingness to intervene to the standard formulation, which is franc-negative and supports the stance. But the market's hike pricing has risen to nearly 50% for December and at least 0.75% by September 2027, so the gap between SNB guidance and market belief is now wide enough that a single meeting resolves it in one direction or the other - a coin flip deserves less confidence than a settled disagreement.

Held tactically with higher confidence, changed strategically. The French budget crisis has escalated - OAT-Bund from a lower base to a one-year high of 111.2bp with a EUR 54bn vote pending - which strengthens the tactical Bullish case. Strategically the Iran war has moved toward settlement rather than escalation, with Middle East crude exports recovering to just under 80% of the pre-war baseline and the dispute reduced to sequencing, and a settlement would be doubly franc-negative, so the strategic stance flattens to Neutral.

Changed strategically, from Bullish to Neutral, and confidence raised substantially on both horizons. The prior Bullish strategic stance attributed FX value to Swiss fiscal quality relative to peers. That transmission runs through the safe-haven and risk channels already counted in Factors 3 and 7, and counting it here as well inflates the weighted score. With AAA ratings from all five agencies unchanged, a zero federal balance and general government debt declining to 38.5% of GDP, the evidence for immateriality is strong, which is why confidence rises to 80 and 74 while the stance goes flat.

Held tactically, changed strategically from Neutral to Bearish. EUR/CHF has moved from 0.93758 on 2026-08-28, which was 0.49% below the lower boundary of the five-touch 0.94217-0.95090 band, to 0.94562 INSIDE that band and 29 pips from its 200-week average - a structural advance that now reaches far enough into the strategic horizon to carry a stance rather than a null.

Held tactically with marginally higher confidence, changed strategically from Neutral to Bearish. The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, the broad dollar index rose 1.59% over the month to 120.33, and swap-line usage remains at USD 72mn - abundant but expensive dollars, which is the configuration in which a funding currency loses on both horizons rather than only the near one.

seasonality.pattern: No CHF-specific documented seasonal pattern exists in the framework's list, and none is invented here. The pattern that does apply, and that the framework names for all currencies, is year-end portfolio rebalancing and the turn-of-year funding effect. It matters more for the franc than for most currencies because CHF is a funding currency: balance-sheet constraints at the turn of the year historically widen cross-currency basis and raise the cost of holding short positions in low-yielding currencies, which squeezes funding currencies higher. Reserve balances falling USD 83.6bn in the week to 2026-09-23 and USD 72.0bn over the year, with SOFR already printing at interest on reserve balances rather than below it, make that mechanism more live this year than usual.
seasonality.relevance_window: Inside the strategic horizon only. The effect concentrates in the final two weeks of December 2026 and the first week of January 2027, which falls outside the 2-4 week tactical window and inside the 1-6 month strategic one. It coincides with the 2026-12-09 FOMC, the 2026-12-10 SNB assessment and the 2026-12-17 ECB projections round, so its signal will be hard to separate from policy effects.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: Not quantified. No CHF-specific study of turn-of-year magnitude was located, and the cross-currency basis series that would measure it is unavailable from any free quoted source. The pattern is therefore recorded qualitatively and carries NO weight in either stance or scenario probability; no numerical magnitude is asserted.
seasonality.current_alignment: Mildly adverse to the strategic bearish view and recorded as such. A turn-of-year funding squeeze would lift the franc at precisely the point the SNB meets, so the December cluster carries correlated upside risk for the franc from two independent sources. The signpost that would show it first is SOFR printing more than 5bp above interest on reserve balances, or central bank liquidity swaps rising above USD 5bn from USD 72mn.

assumptions: The pipeline data cache is the source of truth wherever it holds a precise current figure - policy rates, FX levels and derived analytics, CFTC positioning, BIS REER, macro vintages and scheduled central-bank decisions. Deep research supplies narrative, guidance, catalysts and citations around those numbers. The monthly snapshot used for the whole cycle is Data-Cache/2026-10/, whose _fetched.json is stamped 2026-09-30T18:00:05Z - the latest snapshot fetched before the valuation date. No other snapshot was consulted.

CPI figures in the macro comparison table are the latest PUBLISHED monthly or quarterly prints, each dated in the core-measure field, rather than the cache's point-in-time vintages. This is a deliberate departure: the cached CPI vintages for EUR, CHF, NOK and SEK are 2025-Q4 observations nine to ten months old, and the cached CHF value of 0.0601% against an actual August 2026 reading of 0.80% would be actively misleading in a dossier whose central argument concerns the Swiss inflation path. GDP, unemployment and current-account figures ARE taken from the cache vintage store on a point-in-time basis as of 2026-10-01. The two bases are not mixed within a column, and this latest-published-print basis, labelled with its period, is the convention adopted for the whole 2026-10-01 cycle.

Swiss sovereign yields are LIVE prints - 2Y 0.31% (2026-09-29) and 10Y 0.58% (2026-09-30) - not the cache's monthly IRLTLT01 series. The cached CHF 10Y of 0.47% as of 2026-08-01 is 11bp below the live print and is used for no spread anywhere in this dossier. Live prints are likewise used for Germany (3.63%), France (4.74%) and the United States (2Y 4.89%, 10Y 5.26%). Peer 10-year yields for the United Kingdom, Japan, Australia, Canada, Norway and Sweden remain the cache's MONTHLY series with as-of dates from 2026-06-01 to 2026-08-01, quoted with those dates; given that US 10s rose 51bp in the month to 2026-09-28, those monthly levels understate current yields and therefore understate CHF's yield disadvantage.

The PPP deviation table is NOT a purchasing-power-parity calculation. No PPP exchange-rate series exists in the cache and none was located. The ten entries are a clearly labelled REER-RELATIVE PROXY computed as (CHF REER / peer REER - 1) on the 2026-08 BIS broad real basis. The JPY entry of +51.27% is a base-period artefact of the yen's real depreciation (REER 66.02, -6.50% over one year) and is flagged in the table itself rather than read as a CHF overvaluation signal.

Forward outrights for USD/CHF and EUR/CHF are DERIVED, not quoted. No quoted forward points were located for either pair. The outrights are extrapolated linearly from the cache's futures-implied roll premium - -457.8bp annualised for USD/CHF and -298.7bp for EUR/CHF, both observed 2026-09-25 on a 79.7-to-170.7-day tenor - and are labelled derived at every use. That roll embeds the cross-currency basis, which the cache states cannot be separated from the rate differential: at -457.8bp against a -387.5bp policy spread, the 70.3bp wedge bounds basis plus term effects jointly.

USD/CHF implied volatility is a QUOTED CME at-the-money surface observed 2026-09-25 (41.7d 6.740%, 104.7d 6.662%, 195.7d 6.934%). EUR/CHF implied volatility of 3.212% at three months is a cache TRIANGLE ESTIMATE derived from realised correlations because no listed option exists on that cross, and is labelled an estimate wherever used. The two are not treated as equivalent evidence.

The 25-delta one-month risk reversal is UNAVAILABLE for both USD/CHF and EUR/CHF. No free quoted source was located and Investing.com's USD/CHF options page renders its surface in a widget that returns no figures to retrieval. No value is estimated. Factor 9's confidence is lowered on both horizons for the gap, and the skew judgement in the Expression Assessment rests on the currency's documented history rather than on current pricing.

The one-year implied-volatility percentile of 35 and the BIS REER historical percentile of 42 are ESTIMATES, not published ranks. The cache holds no implied-volatility history and carries only the current REER period with a one-year change. Both are labelled estimates wherever they appear.

Cross-currency basis for 3M EUR/USD, JPY/USD, GBP/USD and CHF/USD is UNAVAILABLE from any free quoted source. The only 2026-dated article located contains illustrative stress ranges of 50-200bp rather than market quotes and was rejected rather than quoted. Factor 10's funding assessment rests instead on SOFR, interest on reserve balances, reserve balances, the Federal Reserve balance sheet, swap-line usage and the broad dollar index, and the factor's strategic confidence is lowered accordingly.
Swiss sovereign CDS spreads at 5 and 10 years are UNAVAILABLE from any free quoted source. Factor 8's sovereign assessment rests on the five agency ratings and the Confederation curve instead.

The Citi Economic Surprise Index for Switzerland is proprietary and was not available. It is substituted by a direct tally of the 23 Swiss events released in the cached 2026-09 calendar window using the vendor's own economic-direction flag: six positive (retail sales, procure.ch PMI, CPI year on year, CPI month on month, GDP quarter on quarter, PPI month on month) and zero negative, with the remainder neutral or unforecast. The method is stated rather than the result being presented as an index value. The vendor's own importance field is US-centric and was not used as a filter.

The SNB Nominal Effective Exchange Rate, named in the currency brief as CHF's secondary index, is not in the cache and no free current series was located. The BIS real effective exchange rate at 99.87 for 2026-08 is substituted and the substitution is disclosed; it is corroborated by the SNB's own statement that the franc depreciated approximately 3% trade-weighted since June 2026.

No Swiss terms-of-trade index is cached and none was located as a current series. The direction of travel is inferred from two sourced components that point in opposite directions - Brent near USD 100, 4.75% higher over September, and Swiss producer and import prices at -0.70% year on year - for an economy that imports energy and exports high-value manufactures, so the net direction is assessed as flat to modestly adverse. The inference is stated as an inference.

CFTC positioning percentiles are WITHIN-SAMPLE ranks over the cached 2026-04-07 to 2026-09-22 tranches, not 1-year, 3-year or 5-year distributions, and are labelled estimates. The 2026-09-22 tranche is 9 days old at the valuation date but is the latest print in existence - the next release falls 2026-10-02 - so it is treated as current, and the vendor non-commercial series released 2026-09-25 at -26,800 corroborates it.

New Zealand's core figure is the RBNZ sectoral factor model, the RBNZ's preferred underlying measure, at 2.7% for 2026-Q2, unchanged from Q1 and released 2026-07-21 [40]; the headline 4.06% is the 2026-Q2 cache vintage. The first build of this dossier repeated the headline in the core column as a documented gap; that is corrected. Singapore has no cached vintages at all - it is not an OECD member - so its GDP (1.40% quarter on quarter and 5.90% year on year, 2026-Q2), CPI, unemployment (1.9%, 2026-Q2) and current-account (16.70% of GDP, 2025) figures are research-sourced [37].

Market-implied Fed path probabilities are taken from CME FedWatch as reported on 2026-09-30: approximately 47% for a 25bp hike at the 2026-10-28 meeting and approximately 90% for at least one hike by year-end, corroborated by a Polymarket contract at 81% and by a separate report putting October odds near 50% after New York Fed President John Williams's remarks. The verification pass lowered Factor 1 confidence from 76/66 to 74/64 and Factor 10 from 62/56 to 60/54 because the corrected figures make the dollar-rate tailwind weaker than first assessed.

Four further sources were rejected outright during research - one stating the SNB policy rate was 1.00% in July 2026, one Fed probability page with internally contradictory figures, and two articles describing a December 2025 SNB decision as though current - and none is cited.

VERIFICATION NOTE: on re-check on 2026-10-05 the cited page shows only its post-valuation quote (USD 102.09 on 2026-10-05, +5.08% on the month, +55.94% on the year), so the 2026-10-01 print of USD 100.17 is the cycle's captured value - identical to the figure used by the NOK and SEK dossiers - and is presented as best available, flagged. Policy rates are the most recent decision actuals in the cached calendar event store, cross-checked against Trading Economics [21]: AUD 4.60% (RBA, 2026-09-29), CAD 2.25%, CHF 0.00%, EUR 2.50% deposit facility rate (main refinancing rate 2.65%), GBP 3.75%, JPY 1.25% (BoJ, 2026-09-18), NOK 4.50% (Norges Bank, 2026-09-24), NZD 2.75%, SEK 1.75%, and USD 3.875% as the effective midpoint of the 3.75-4.00% target range (upper bound 4.00%, a 400bp spread to CHF on that basis). Spreads in this dossier are on the deposit-rate and effective-midpoint conventions unless stated. SGD has no policy rate - MAS manages an S$NEER band - so no SGD spread is computed; the SGD dossier of this cycle uses the 6-month T-bill at 1.92% as a proxy. The cached CBPOL_AU and CBPOL_NO series and the CBPOL_JP tail, all of which end before the September hikes, were NOT used, and the first build's AUD, NOK and JPY policy rates, which were one hike stale, have been corrected throughout.

Prices are point-in-time to the cycle: spot, moving averages, ATR, zones and realised volatility are the gated store's analytics as captured at first build (2026-09-29 close). The derived pair files refreshed on 2026-10-05 carry a 2026-10-02 bar and were used only for their corrected rates blocks, not for prices. Swiss September CPI (1.0% year on year) and the procure.ch PMI (55.3) were released at 06:30 and 07:30 UTC on 2026-10-01, after the cycle's data cut, and are recorded as post-valuation context only; a 1.0% headline print would meet the tactical conviction ladder's decrease-to-2 condition and is the first thing the next cycle must assess.

Phase 6 verification was executed DIRECTLY rather than by a subagent, because no subagent-spawning tool (Agent or Task) exists in this execution environment. All 40 citations were retrieved and confirmed to resolve and to support the claims carried. Three figures were corrected and two source-internal inconsistencies were recorded. The corrections: Fed path probabilities were replaced with CME FedWatch figures (October approximately 47%, at least one 2026 hike approximately 90%) after an earlier source quoting 68% and 95% proved uncorroborated, and Factor 1 and Factor 10 confidence were each cut by 2 points on both horizons as a result, moving the tactical net score from -0.3000 to -0.2930 and the strategic from -0.2566 to -0.2494; the Swiss September CPI release was confirmed as still unpublished at the valuation date and its published month-on-month consensus of 0.0% was added; and the German Bund yield was cross-checked at 3.58% on 2026-09-30 against 3.63% on 2026-09-29, confirming the CHF-Bund spread within 5bp. The 2026-10-05 rebuild re-ran the gate on every changed figure - peer policy rates, carry ratios, the macro table core rows, Brent and the rankings - and corrected an arithmetic misstatement of Hormuz recovery (9.719mn b/d is about half the 19.513mn b/d baseline; the just-under-80% figure refers to regional crude exports); details are in the run log.

Two source-internal inconsistencies were found during verification and are resolved in favour of the pipeline cache, which is authoritative for these figures. The Swiss inflation page reports an August month-on-month figure of 0.40% in its data field while its prose text says 0.1%; the cached calendar records the 2026-09-03 release as +0.4% actual against a 0.0% forecast and -0.1% previous, and 0.40% is used. The Swiss 2-year note page reports 0.31% in its data field while its prose says the yield eased to 0.32% on 2026-09-29; the 1bp difference is immaterial and 0.31% is used, with the +19bp monthly change unaffected either way.

The seasonality section records the framework's generic year-end rebalancing pattern with NO quantified magnitude, because no CHF-specific study was located and the cross-currency basis series that would measure it is unavailable. It carries zero weight in any stance or scenario probability.
